name: Clean Hands
description: A Vantablack subsidiary thriller in which you play Investigator Dakarai Shen-Petrov, an elite corporate crimes detective hired by a Tier 5 consortium to track a runner cell accused of sabotaging automated supply chains. The film is engineered for maximum moral comfort — the protagonist's methods are brutal but the game is rigged so the player always feels justified. Neural feedback systems are calibrated to suppress guilt responses during scenes of interrogation and violence, a technique that became standard in Vantablack action product.
cultural_impact: Clean Hands is credited with hardening Tier 2-3 attitudes toward Shelf runners during a period of heightened corporate enforcement, and is studied in media ethics courses as a case study in neural-feed emotional engineering.
story_hooks: The runner cell depicted in the film was real; one surviving member wants the world to see the unedited security footage that contradicts the film's version of events.
A neural-feed technician who worked on the guilt-suppression calibration is suffering a crisis of conscience and is leaking the proprietary suppression code to underground media.
The party is hired to find a Tier 3 viewer who, instead of being emotionally dampened by Clean Hands, was somehow sensitized — and now cannot stop experiencing other people's pain.
